From: Anika Rao <anika.rao@medservices.com>

Date: 2025-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Processing territory & DPA onboarding - initial SSQ + diagrams

Hi Karthik / Lauren,

Thanks for picking this up. We're starting the DPA onboarding for our upcoming pilot and need to reconcile a couple of items for privacy/security review before procurement will clear the contract. High-level asks:  

- Confirm which Redwood subprocessors will see unredacted PII in the EU processing path and whether any are outside the EU.
- Annotated dataflow diagram that shows where patient identifiers are ingested, tokenized/pseudonymized, stored, and where model telemetry (inference logs) are retained.
- A short access matrix: which Redwood roles (engineers, ops, on-call, support) have read/write access to PII or keys.
- Clarify onshore-only / residency constraints: can processing for EU patients be restricted to EU-only inference? If so, how is that enforced (routing/fallbacks)?

I've attached our initial questionnaire (MedServices_Onboarding_Questions.xlsx) with numbered items. Procurement (cc'd Tom) also flagged they may need an annex in the DPA for processing territory carveouts — do you have a template or suggested language?

Can we get the annotated diagram + role matrix by EOD Tuesday? If not, a 30-min sync this week works.

Thanks,
Anika Rao
Privacy Lead, MedServices Health
anika.rao@medservices.com
Attachments: MedServices_Onboarding_Questions.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika.rao@medservices.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Processing territory & DPA onboarding - initial SSQ + diagrams

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear list and the workbook. Short answers up front and proposed next steps below.

Summary answers:
- Subprocessors: We will provide a definitive list in the annotated dataflow. At a high level: infra providers (cloud hosting in-region), logging/monitoring vendor (redacted telemetry), and a managed KMS partner for key escrow. We'll flag which subprocessors have potential access to unredacted data and which only see hashed/tokenized payloads.
- Annotated dataflow & access matrix: attaching an initial pass (redwood_annotated_dataflow_v1.pdf) showing ingress, tokenization layer, model inference, telemetry capture points, and storage tiers. Access matrix included on page 3.
- Residency: Yes — we support EU-only inference routing via our Private & Dedicated deployment options. For Hosted, we provide regional routing controls and can enforce EU-only routing for a customer bucket; we also document fallbacks and automatic model-variant routing when capacity is constrained. Enforcement is via network zoning + routing policy in the control plane and audit logs for proof.

Next steps and schedule:
- I've attached the v1 diagram and flagged items that need your confirmation.
- Please mark questions 4, 7, and 12 in your workbook as high priority; they map to tokenization, KMS custody, and residency enforcement.
- I'm available for a 30-min sync Thu 07/24 09:00-09:30 PT or Fri 07/25 14:00-14:30 PT — happy to coordinate with Tom for procurement presence.

I'll follow up with a short note on suggested DPA annex language (procurement-friendly) and paste a high-level subprocessors table in that message.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security & Privacy Manager | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood_annotated_dataflow_v1.pdf

To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-20T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Processing territory & DPA onboarding - initial SSQ + diagrams

Karthik / Lauren — quick procurement question while you prepare the artifacts: for EU patient data we need an explicit statement of whether processing (inference + temporary KV cache) can be restricted to EU-only infrastructure with no failover to US regions. If Redwood's hosted tier could route to a US fallback automatically, procurement will require contract language preventing that for the EU cohort. Is that supported today on the Hosted plan or would we need Dedicated/Private for a hard guarantee? Also curious about auditability — what evidence will we receive that proves residency (logs, traceroute, workload region id)?

If you can add the residency proof items into the diagram or as an annex that would be ideal.

Tom Ellis
Senior Procurement Manager, MedServices Health
tom.ellis@medservices.com

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika.rao@medservices.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medservices.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-20T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Processing territory & DPA onboarding - initial SSQ + diagrams

Hi Anika / Tom — looping in Rafael so leadership is aware of residency/contract asks. Quick clarifications and asks from our side: 

- Residency guarantees: Hosted (multi-tenant) provides strong regional routing but cannot legally guarantee absolute hard failover prevention; for contractual guarantees you will want Dedicated or Private (we can add a DPA annex that requires Dedicated capacity pinned to EU regions).
- Auditability: we provide an evidence bundle that includes per-request region metadata, routing decision logs, and a signed KMS custody statement. We'll include a sample export (CSV + signed manifest) in the onboarding evidence pack.
- Subprocessor exposure: the attached diagram marks subprocessors that could access unredacted payloads. For customers requiring additional shielding, we recommend either (a) Dedicated with customer-managed KMS, or (b) Private deployment (VPC) with HSM/KMS in-customer-control.

Proposed DPA annex language (draft):
"Redwood shall deploy Customer Processing for specified EU Customer Subpopulations exclusively within EU regions and shall not route such processing to non-EU regions without Customer's prior written consent. Dedicated or Private deployment modes shall be used where Customer requires contractual residency guarantees; Hosted routing options are control-plane enforced but may permit emergency fallback when explicitly authorized by Redwood operations and notified to the Customer."

I've uploaded a draft annex and a DocuSign envelope for routing the DPA changes: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456789 and shared the onboarding evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-example-dataflow.

Next steps: Karthik will push a cleaned annotated diagram (v1 -> v1.1) and a short subprocessor table by tomorrow morning; if that looks good we can loop Legal and Procurement to redline the annex.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Attachments: DPA_Annex_Territory_Draft.docx
